verses.1: A prayer of David. Hear, O LORD, my righteousness, listen to my plea. Attend to my prayer that does not come from deceitful lips.
verses.2: Let my judgment come forth before your face; let your eyes behold what is upright.
verses.3: You have tested my heart, searched me in the night. You have refined me, and found no deceit in me.
verses.4: I have not allowed the words of mortals to reach my mouth; I have kept the ways of the violent in check.
verses.5: You have set my feet upon your pathways, so that my steps do not falter.
verses.6: I have called to you, for you have answered me, O God. Turn your ear to me, hear my words.
verses.7: Wondrous is your steadfast love, O Savior, to those who take refuge, from the right hand of those who rise up against them.
verses.8: Keep me as the apple of the eye; under the shadow of your wings, hide me.
verses.9: From the face of the wicked who have persecuted me—my enemies, who encircle my life—
verses.10: their fat is closed up; their mouths speak with pride.
verses.11: Now they have cast out and surrounded me; their eyes are set to cast me down to the earth.
verses.12: Like a lion ready to pounce, like a young lion lurking in hiding.
verses.13: Arise, O LORD, confront them, bring them low. Rescue my life from the wicked with your sword.
verses.14: From the hands of your enemies, O LORD, deliver them from the earth. Divide their portion among the living, and let the hidden ones fill their bellies; let their children be satisfied, and leave their wealth to their infants.
verses.15: But I, in righteousness, shall behold your face; I shall be satisfied when I awake in your likeness.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 4: The phrase "I have kept the ways of the violent in check" reflects the meaning of "ar'hot paritz" as ways of the violent or of the wicked.  
- v. 14: "Let the hidden ones" is a poetic rendering of "mi-mitim," which may literally mean "from the hidden ones" but is used here to refer to the wicked or conspirators.  
- v. 15: "In your likeness" is a poetic rendering of "temunat'kha" to capture the idea of being transformed or renewed in the image of God.
